holidays.name: National Veggie Burger Day
holidays.description: A salute to the plant-powered patty. Black bean, chickpea, mushroom, lentil and beet versions all get their moment on the bun. Even devoted carnivores are invited to try one.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance. It has been celebrated on June 5 by veggie fans and restaurants. The modern veggie burger is often traced to Gregory Sams, who sold his VegeBurger in London in the 1980s.
holidays.funFact: Gregory Sams's VegeBurger started as a dry mix that you rehydrated at home. It later became a supermarket staple in the UK.

holidays.name: Hot Air Balloon Day
holidays.description: A day to look up and celebrate the colorful, drifting giants of the sky. Balloonists, dreamers and picnic-with-a-view fans mark it with launches and festivals.
holidays.origin: The day honors the dawn of human flight. In 1783 the Montgolfier brothers of France publicly demonstrated their hot air balloon, and it rose into the sky above Annonay.
holidays.funFact: The first passengers in a Montgolfier balloon were not people. They were a sheep, a duck and a rooster, who flew in a test over Versailles later in 1783.

holidays.name: National Gingerbread Day
holidays.description: A spicy-sweet day for gingerbread cookies, cakes and houses. You can bake some, nibble some, or build a tiny edible cottage and then eat the roof.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. Gingerbread itself dates back centuries in Europe, where it was sold at fairs and festivals.
holidays.funFact: Queen Elizabeth I is said to have served gingerbread figures made to look like her guests and visiting dignitaries.
